newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Deportees in Kuwait prison end hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Deportees in Kuwait prison end hunger strike.

text.p: Prisoners in a Kuwaiti deportation centre have ended a hunger strike, al-Seyassah newspaper reported on Tuesday.
An official confirmed the report but gave no further details.

The newspaper said the interior ministry had "managed to control incidents at the Talha centre" and that prison life had returned to normal after the hunger-strikers were treated at al-Farwanya hospital.
Some were treated for wounds inflicted on themselves with shaving tools, the newspaper said. Five of the injured were under investigation, it added.

Talha, set up after the 1991 Gulf crisis, houses foreigners suspected of violating national security, as well as those who lack work permits and criminals who have completed prison terms and are awaiting deportation.
The newspaper quoted a relative of a prisoner as saying about 60 stateless people had gone on hunger strike on Saturday to demand their temporary release.
Kuwait has said it plans to shut the centre and give its inmates a three-month release to help them sort out residency status irregularities, according to media reports.

But al-Seyassah quoted Major General Fahd al-Fahd, an interior ministry assistant undersecretary, as saying that most of the hunger strikers and other offenders could not be released because they had cooperated with Iraqi occupation forces after the 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
